sections.skill: Plan interview questions about past behavior

questions.prompt: Which interview question gives the most reliable information?

choices.text: Would you hire a tutor if I offered one next year?
Do you think tutoring is a good idea for most kids?
How much would you be willing to pay for my service?
When did you last hire a tutor, and how did you find one?

questions.correct_answer: When did you last hire a tutor, and how did you find one?
questions.intro: A customer interview is a short conversation to learn about someone's real problems. The most useful questions ask about what people already DID, not what they say they WOULD do. "Tell me about the last time you looked for a babysitter" gives real facts: how long it took, what they paid, what went wrong. "Would you use my babysitting app?" invites polite guesses. Past behavior is better evidence than predictions, because people are often too kind or too hopeful about the future.
questions.feedback: Asking about a recent real event gives facts instead of guesses.

People often guess kindly or hopefully.

questions.intro: Compare two questions about gyms. "Would you go to the gym three times a week?" Most people say yes, even if they rarely go. "How many times did you go to the gym last week?" gets a real number. The first question measures hope. The second measures behavior. When you test a business idea, behavior is what pays the bills, so ask "did" questions whenever you can.
